about.title: Monterey Park Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey Park's mix of dense commercial corridors, shopping plazas, and older apartment complexes near Garfield Avenue and Garvey Avenue means uneven walkways, wet floors, and poorly lit stairwells are common hazards. When a property owner fails to notice or fix a dangerous condition, California law may hold them responsible for resulting injuries. But proving that a business or landlord knew or reasonably should have known about a hazard takes evidence gathered quickly, before spills get mopped up and surveillance footage gets erased. LawProactive connects people injured in falls anywhere in Monterey Park, from Atlantic Boulevard storefronts to SR-60 corridor businesses, with an independent attorney who can evaluate the circumstances of the fall and help pursue a fair claim. This is a free connection service; there's no cost or obligation to see if a case might move forward, and any attorney matched works on contingency, meaning fees only apply if there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Documentation Matters in a Monterey Park Fall Case

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Monterey Park businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of video can be critical to reconstructing what happened.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you were partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced share of damages rather than being shut out entirely.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Monterey Park?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity, such as a city building or public sidewalk, the deadline is much shorter and requires a separate claims process. It's best to speak with an attorney as soon as possible to avoid missing any deadline.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Atlantic Boulevard or Garvey Avenue and didn't report it right away?
items.answer: Not reporting immediately doesn't automatically end your options, but it can make proving the hazard existed more difficult. Photos of the scene, witness names, and any available surveillance footage become even more important. An independent attorney can help figure out what evidence may still be recoverable.

items.question: Does it cost anything to find out if I have a case?
items.answer: No. LawProactive's connection service is free, and there's no obligation to move forward. If matched with an attorney, they typically work on contingency, meaning you pay nothing upfront and fees apply only if you recover compensation.
